claims.text: Ti40Ni40Nb10V10 qualifies as a high-entropy alloy under the compositional definition stated in the query.
Conventionally cast Ti40Ni40Nb10V10 has coarse microstructural features, elemental segregation, and equilibrium precipitates.
The proposed LPBF parameters can produce cooling rates greater than 10^5 K/s in Ti40Ni40Nb10V10.
LPBF followed by a 700°C, 30-minute stabilization treatment will produce a homogeneous, refined, metastable single-phase microstructure in Ti40Ni40Nb10V10.
The intervention will suppress elemental segregation in Ti40Ni40Nb10V10.
The intervention will reduce residual defects in the LPBF-processed alloy.
Rapid solidification during LPBF suppresses formation of equilibrium phases.
Rapid solidification during LPBF suppresses elemental segregation.
A brief stabilization heat treatment mitigates LPBF-induced porosity and residual stresses.
The 700°C, 30-minute stabilization treatment maintains the metastable microstructure.
The refined single-phase microstructure enhances solid-solution strengthening.
The resulting microstructure improves resistance to dislocation glide and high-temperature creep.
The stabilized LPBF alloy will have approximately 15–25% greater elevated-temperature specific strength than the conventionally cast alloy.
The stabilized LPBF alloy will have approximately 15–25% greater creep resistance than the conventionally cast alloy.
The strength and creep improvements will occur without significantly compromising ductility.
The predicted improvement remains applicable at service temperatures up to approximately 800°C.
Excessive stabilization temperature or duration may cause unintended phase transformations.
LPBF of the analogous WTaMoNbV alloy has been demonstrated to be feasible and to yield a single BCC solid solution with properties and microstructure similar to an arc-melted counterpart.

contradictions.description: The query requires at least five elements, each at 5–35 at%, but Ti40Ni40Nb10V10 contains only four elements and has Ti and Ni at 40 at% each. It therefore does not satisfy the stated compositional definition.
